name: Sun (Sol)
notableFacts: Our home star! Currently fusing hydrogen into helium via the p-p chain; hosts 8 planets with Earth situated in the liquid water habitable zone.

name: Sirius A
notableFacts: The brightest star in Earth's night sky. Part of a binary system with white dwarf companion Sirius B.

name: Sirius B (The Pup)
notableFacts: One of the first white dwarfs discovered. Earth-sized (~5,800 km radius) but containing 1.02 Solar masses, supported by quantum electron degeneracy pressure.

name: Cygnus X-1 (HDE 226868)
notableFacts: The first confirmed stellar-mass black hole (~21.2 M☉). Fused matter accreting from this O-supergiant companion reaches 10,000,000 K, radiating intense relativistic X-rays and twin astrophysical plasma jets.

name: Crab Pulsar (PSR B0531+21)
notableFacts: City-sized spinning sphere of nuclear matter (~11 km radius, 1.4 M☉) born in the historical supernova of 1054 AD. Spins 30.2 times per second, generating magnetic fields of 4 trillion Gauss.

name: RX J1856.5-3754 (Magnificent Seven)
notableFacts: The closest known isolated neutron star (~400 ly). Emits pure thermal blackbody radiation from its solid iron/neutron crust without any radio pulsar beam.

name: Betelgeuse
notableFacts: Colossal red supergiant nearing the end of its life. If placed at the center of our solar system, its pulsating atmosphere would engulf the orbit of Jupiter!

name: Rigel
notableFacts: Luminous blue supergiant star in Orion; outshines the Sun by over 120,000 times.

name: Vega
notableFacts: Historical photometric standard star (0 magnitude, B-V = 0.00). Surrounded by a prominent circumstellar debris disk with a candidate giant planet.

name: Proxima Centauri
notableFacts: The closest known star to the Solar System (4.24 ly). Hosts Proxima b, an Earth-mass terrestrial exoplanet inside its circumstellar habitable zone.

name: TRAPPIST-1
notableFacts: Famous ultra-cool red dwarf hosting 7 Earth-sized terrestrial planets in compact resonant orbits, with three (e, f, g) inside the temperate habitable zone.

name: Kepler-186
notableFacts: Hosts Kepler-186f, the first confirmed Earth-radius exoplanet discovered orbiting within the habitable zone of another star (NASA Kepler, 2014).

name: Arcturus
notableFacts: Brightest star in northern celestial hemisphere. A preview of what our Sun will look like in ~5 billion years when it ascends the Red Giant Branch.

name: Aldebaran
notableFacts: The 'Eye of Taurus', an orange giant that has exhausted core hydrogen and swollen to 44 solar radii.

name: Polaris (North Star)
notableFacts: Earth's northern pole star. Located inside the Instability Strip, Polaris pulsates with a period of ~3.97 days.

name: Antares
notableFacts: The 'Heart of the Scorpion', a pulsating red supergiant over 680 times wider than the Sun.

name: Spica
notableFacts: A massive, very hot spectroscopic binary rotating so rapidly that the stars are gravitationally distorted into egg shapes.

name: Deneb
notableFacts: One of the most intrinsically luminous stars visible to the human eye, with ~200,000 times the radiant power of the Sun.

name: Pollux
notableFacts: The closest giant star to the Sun and the brightest star known to host an extrasolar planet (Thestias / Pollux b).

name: Barnard's Star
notableFacts: Fastest moving star in the sky (proper motion ~10.3 arcsec/year). Second closest star system to the Sun.

name: Eta Carinae
notableFacts: One of the most massive stellar systems in our galaxy, shining with 5,000,000 Solar luminosities. Erupting into the Homunculus Nebula; candidate pair-instability supernova.

notableFacts: Hosts Teegarden b & c, two temperate Earth-mass planets in the habitable zone with high Earth Similarity Index (ESI > 0.9).

name: KELT-9
notableFacts: Hottest known exoplanet host star; its ultra-hot giant KELT-9b reaches day-side temperatures of 4,600 K, hotter than most stars!

name: WASP-76
notableFacts: Famous ultra-hot world where iron vaporizes on the day-side (2,400°C) and condenses into liquid iron raindrops on the night-side.

name: Kepler-22
notableFacts: Kepler-22b was the first transiting exoplanet confirmed by NASA's Kepler mission in the habitable zone of a Sun-like star (2011).

name: Kepler-452
notableFacts: Nicknamed 'Earth's Older Cousin'; Kepler-452b is a super-Earth orbiting in the habitable zone of a 6-billion-year-old G2V star.

name: Kepler-442
notableFacts: Hosts Kepler-442b, scientifically regarded as one of the most promising habitable exoplanets, receiving ~70% of Earth's sunlight.

name: Kepler-16
notableFacts: The first confirmed circumbinary planet: Kepler-16b orbits two stars simultaneously, akin to the fictional planet Tatooine.

name: Pi Mensae
notableFacts: Naked-eye yellow dwarf hosting a sub-Neptune (Pi Men c, discovered by TESS) and an eccentric super-Jupiter (Pi Men b).

name: Gliese 436
notableFacts: Warm Neptune (Gliese 436 b) surrounded by an enormous, comet-like evaporating cloud of hydrogen gas trailing behind its orbit.

name: HD 219134
notableFacts: Brightest naked-eye star confirmed to host transiting rocky super-Earths, located just 21 light-years away in Cassiopeia.

name: HD 10180
notableFacts: Rich planetary architecture discovered by the HARPS spectrograph; hosts at least six planets with masses ranging from Neptune to Saturn.

name: Gliese 12
notableFacts: Discovered in 2024: hosts Gliese 12 b, a temperate Earth-sized world (R = 0.96 R⊕) receiving solar irradiance comparable to Venus.

name: TOI-715
notableFacts: Discovered in 2024 by TESS: hosts TOI-715 b, a 1.55 Earth-radius super-Earth situated inside the conservative liquid water habitable zone.

name: Gliese 367 (Tahar)
notableFacts: Hosts Tahar (GJ 367 b), an ultra-dense iron-rich sub-Earth that completes an entire orbit around its sun in just 7.7 hours.

name: TOI-178
notableFacts: Spectacular orbital resonance: five of its six planets form an unbroken 18:9:6:4:3 resonant chain with densities varying wildly.

name: TOI-849
notableFacts: First confirmed remnant core of an evaporated gas giant (Chthonian planet) situated in the 'Hot Neptune Desert'.

name: LP 791-18
notableFacts: Hosts LP 791-18 d, a temperate Earth-sized world experiencing intense tidal heating that triggers widespread volcanic activity like Jupiter's moon Io.

name: AU Microscopii
notableFacts: Young (22 Myr) flare star surrounded by an edge-on debris disc with fast-moving ripples and two transiting Neptune-sized planets.

name: 16 Cygni B
notableFacts: Solar analogue component of a triple star system; hosts a Jupiter-mass planet in a highly eccentric orbit (e = 0.68) shaped by Kozai resonance.

name: HD 106906
notableFacts: Hosts a directly imaged 11-Jupiter mass companion orbiting at an astonishing distance of 650 AU, analog to the hypothesized Solar System 'Planet Nine'.
